messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Automated Electrotransformation of Escherichia coli on a Digital Microfluidic Platform Using Bioactivated Magnetic Beads (bead-based preparation of electrocompetent cells, heat-shock induction, DI-water media exchange, oligonucleotide loading, on-cartridge electroporation, and recovery for a multiplex automated genome engineering, MAGE, cycle)

REAGENTS USED:
  - E. coli Culture (EcNR2 DmutS lambda-Red+ strain, grown to stationary phase then sampled at mid-log phase, OD600 4.5-6.0)
  - Magnetic Beads (Wheat Germ Agglutinin, WGA, lectin-coated streptavidin superparamagnetic beads, 1 um diameter, for cell binding)
  - Blocking Agent (fat-free powdered milk, 2.5 mg/mL, to prevent in-droplet bead-cell clumping)
  - Growth Medium (defined MOPS EZ medium supplemented with biotin, or LB, used for growth, heat shock, and recovery)
  - Wash Buffer (DI water with 0.05% Tween 20, used for repeated media-exchange washes to make cells electrocompetent)
  - Oligo Reagent (90-nucleotide single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide, e.g. bla-restore ODN, introduced for lambda-Red-mediated allelic replacement)
  - Recovery Medium (growth medium added immediately after the electroporation pulse for cell recovery and outgrowth)

STEPS:
1. Bead binding: mix the mid-log-phase E. coli culture with WGA-lectin-coated magnetic beads and rotate/incubate for 15 minutes to bind cells to beads (approximately one bead per cell).
2. Bead blocking: mix the bead-bound cells with fat-free powdered milk blocking agent for 1 minute to prevent bead-cell aggregation and promote uniform dispersion.
3. Media exchange: pull bound cells out of suspension with a magnet, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the bead-bound cells in growth medium.
4. Heat-shock induction: incubate the resuspended, bead-bound cells at 42 C for 15 minutes to induce expression of the lambda-Red recombination proteins (Exo, Beta, Gam).
5. Electrocompetence washes: for each of 3 wash cycles, magnetically pellet the bound cells, remove the supernatant, and replace it with DI water (with 0.05% Tween 20) without resuspension, to render the cells electrocompetent.
6. Oligo loading: suspend the washed, bead-bound cells in DI water, add the single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide, and incubate briefly (about 30 seconds) to allow oligo uptake.
7. Temperature control and electroporation: hold the sample at the target pulse temperature (4 C or room temperature, depending on protocol variant) and apply a high-field-strength electroporation pulse (up to 24-26 kV/cm, RC time constant approximately 5-6 ms) to transiently permeabilize the cell membrane and deliver the oligonucleotide into the cells.
8. Recovery: immediately merge the pulsed sample with recovery growth medium and incubate at 30 C for 2.5 hours to allow the cells to recover and express any successfully incorporated genetic changes.
9. Transformation frequency readout: plate (or otherwise assay) the recovered cell sample on selective and non-selective media to determine the transformation frequency as the ratio of colony-forming units on the selective condition to the total colony-forming units.

INTERPRETATION: Successful automated electrotransformation is confirmed by transformation frequencies comparable to conventional benchtop cuvette electroporation (up to 21-22% on both benchtop and the microfluidic device), adequate cell retention through the bead-based preparation (about 15% retention through the full MAGE preparation, 82% through gentle washing alone), and reproducible on-cartridge MAGE cycling with typical device frequencies averaging 9%, supporting the feasibility of fully automated, iterative genome engineering on a digital microfluidic platform.

manifest ecoli_culture

manifest recovery_medium

instructions:

cells = dispense 1 units of ecoli_culture
beads = dispense 1 units of magnetic_beads
bound = mix cells with beads for 900s

milk = dispense 1 units of blocking_agent
blocked = mix bound with milk for 60s

media = dispense 1 units of growth_medium
suspended = mix blocked with media for 15s

heat suspended at 42c for 900s

repeat 3 times {
    wash = dispense 1 units of wash_buffer
    suspended = mix suspended with wash for 15s
    dispose suspended
}

oligo = dispense 1 units of oligo_reagent
electrocompetent = mix suspended with oligo for 30s

heat electrocompetent at 4c for 60s
heat electrocompetent at 24c for 5s

recovery = dispense 1 units of recovery_medium
recovered = mix electrocompetent with recovery for 15s

heat recovered at 30c for 9000s

cfu_reading = detect fluorescence on recovered for 60s

dispose recovered

metadata.protocol_name: Automated Electrotransformation of Escherichia coli on a Digital Microfluidic Platform Using Bioactivated Magnetic Beads (Moore et al. 2017)

sources.title: Automated Electrotransformation of Escherichia coli on a Digital Microfluidic Platform Using Bioactivated Magnetic Beads

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the paper's Figure 4 benchtop electroporation-optimization protocol (Section II.C, 'Electrotransformation optimization'), which was designed to be reproducible using available digital microfluidic platform functions and was subsequently ported on-cartridge (Section III.C, 'Microfluidic trials'). It covers WGA-lectin magnetic-bead binding of mid-log E. coli (15 min), fat-free-powdered-milk bead blocking (1 min), magnet-based media exchange into growth medium, 42C/15-min heat-shock induction of lambda-Red recombination proteins, three DI-water electrocompetence washes with magnetic pelleting, oligo loading and brief incubation, an electroporation pulse, and a 30C/2.5h recovery step. Because BioScript's grammar has no dedicated electroporation or magnet-actuation primitive, the electroporation pulse is modeled with two 'heat' instructions (one representing pre-pulse temperature control at 4C, one at an illustrative 24C/5s standing in for the high-field-strength kV/cm pulse itself), reusing 'heat' as the only temperature/energy-delivery instruction available -- the same convention used in the earlier pyrosequencing translation where 'detect fluorescence' stood in for a non-fluorescence readout. Likewise, 'detect fluorescence on recovered' stands in for the paper's CFU-plating-based transformation-frequency readout (Eq. 3), since BioScript exposes no colony-counting primitive. The repeat-3 wash block models the three DI-water washes described in Figure 4 step 8, not the full benchtop-vs-bead-bound comparison, the electrostatic dielectric-shielding simulation (Section III.A, Figures 9-10, Table II), the bead-blocking-agent screening across 12 candidate agents (Table I), the EWoD cartridge electrode/hardware design (Figures 5-7), or the on-cartridge software flowchart and droplet-merge video documentation (Figure 12, Figure 13, Supplementary Material) -- these are hardware-design, screening, or validation sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive and are intentionally not modeled; only the core bead-based cell-preparation-to-recovery MAGE cycle is captured here.

chemical_evidence.source_quote: EcNR2 cultures were grown to mid-log phase (OD600 = 4.5-6.0)
Wheat Germ Agglutinin (WGA) lectin was found to be the most effective at mediating binding
fat-free powdered milk at 2.5 mg/ml was chosen for use in the pulse optimization experiments
MOPS EZ supplemented with biotin, which do not contain cell-wall sugars
0.05% Tween 20 was present in all solutions, as it facilitates electrowetting
an oligonucleotide from Integrated DNA Technologies to restore the bla gene
add 1 ml of room-temperature growth medium to cuvette as quickly as possible

operation_evidence.source_quote: 100 ul of coated beads were added to the cell suspension... put on a rotator to bind for 15 min
Add 30 ul of 5.7% fat free powdered milk to the cell solution... Mix the solution for 1 minute
Place the cell sample tube into shaking heat bath of 42 C for 15 minutes

operation_evidence.bs_operation: repeat 3 times { wash = dispense(wash_buffer); mix; dispose }
operation_evidence.source_quote: For each wash, magnetically pellet bound cells. Remove supernatant and replace with 600 ul DI water, without re-suspension
add 1 ml of room-temperature growth medium... Rotate sample at 30 C for 2.5 hours to recover

numeric_mismatches.note: This models the electroporation pulse itself using the 'heat' instruction as a stand-in for a non-thermal high-field-strength electric pulse (paper values: up to 24-26 kV/cm, RC time constant ~5-6 ms); BioScript's grammar exposes no dedicated electroporation primitive, so the numeric value (24) represents kV/cm rather than degrees Celsius, and the duration (5s) is an illustrative placeholder rather than the millisecond-scale RC time constant.

Represents the pre-pulse cold-hold step (cells commonly pulsed at 4C for stability); the exact hold duration before pulsing is not explicitly stated as 60s in the text, this is an illustrative placeholder.

Detection in the paper is colony-forming-unit (CFU) plate counting on LB and LB+Carbenicillin agar (Eq. 3), not a fluorescence measurement; 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect primitive exposed by BioScript's grammar, standing in for the generic transformation-frequency readout.

Matches the 3 DI-water washes in Figure 4 step 8, but does not model the magnet-pelleting/supernatant-removal mechanism itself (no resuspension between washes), since BioScript has no magnet-actuation or partial-droplet-removal primitive; the wash is approximated as a full mix-then-dispose per the pattern used in prior translated protocols.

Approximates the paper's magnet-pull-out-of-suspension, supernatant removal, and resuspension in growth medium (Figure 4, step 5) as a single mix operation, since BioScript has no primitive for partial droplet/supernatant removal distinct from a full merge.
